question: Why do independently sampled crops repeatedly produce Z=DIFFERENT_PROCESS and Y/X=SAME_PROCESS?

H1a_coordinate_or_pair_bug.evidence: Synthetic coordinate tests (tests/test_axis_semantics_geometry.py) confirm the affinity pair is exactly +1 along the affinity axis for all three axes: Z=(z,y,x)<->(z+1,y,x), Y=(z,y,x)<->(z,y+1,x), X=(z,y,x)<->(z,y,x+1). Array order is ZYX throughout (registration/coordinate_frames.json array_order=ZYX); no transpose/flip in pair construction.

H2_voxel_scale_anisotropy.evidence: Source five_yuri_4contrast is isotropic 8x8x8 nm (dvid survey manifest source.voxel_size_nm_xyz=[8,8,8]; registration/coordinate_frames.json voxel_size_nm_xyz=[8,8,8]). A one-voxel step is 8 nm along Z, Y, and X equally. This is NOT anisotropic ssTEM (contrast: registry CREMI 40x4x4).

H1b_interface_context_non_equivariance.evidence: The historical 3-member spread uses other[0] (first axis != affinity axis), so Z-affinity spreads along Y, while Y- and X-affinity both spread along Z. The spread direction is not equivariant across axes.

H1b_as_dominant_cause.evidence: Counterfactual comparison MV-G3-AXIS-CONTEXT-COMPARISON-001 recomputed the axis effect under CENTER_ONLY, HISTORICAL_ASYMMETRIC, and SYMMETRIC_BOTH_ORTHO context constructions. Headline axis_mean_spread is essentially unchanged across constructions (e.g. step: 9.39 / 8.06 / 8.23; ctx_grad: 9.92 / 8.13 / 8.19). Restoring context symmetry does NOT remove the axis effect.

H3_dominant_gradient_candidate_selection.reason: The remaining strongest untested mechanism: edge eligibility is decided by axis = argmax(abs(gradient)) at each candidate, so an axis only becomes reviewable where its gradient dominates. This couples which edges are seen to axis orientation. Phase B tests this directly by defining all three edges at each location independently.

H4_biological_or_acquisition_directional.reason: If axis-neutral eligibility still yields Z=DIFFERENT/Y,X=SAME at the same locations, the effect is intrinsic to Z-adjacent edges (biology/acquisition), not selection.

within_class_center_edge_statistics.source: MV-G3-AXIS-CONTEXT-COMPARISON-001 (raw-only; labels used only to stratify)

single_voxel_intensity_step_means_by_axi.note: From the 'step' construction, HISTORICAL_ASYMMETRIC per_axis means.

within_class_center_edge_statistics.key_observation: Z-DIFFERENT edges occupy a LOW single-voxel intensity-step regime (mean ~7.8) that OVERLAPS the Y/X SAME regime (Y-SAME ~5.1, X-SAME ~4.1), whereas Y/X-DIFFERENT edges sit at a much higher step regime (~52-70). Every reviewed Z edge was DIFFERENT (0 SAME).
within_class_center_edge_statistics.interpretation_caveat: This does NOT by itself prove the expert applied different labeling criteria across axes. A single 1-voxel intensity step is insufficient to characterize the surrounding 3-D biological morphology the reviewer actually judged. It is a raw-signal observation, not a claim about reviewer behavior.

did_not_modify: any prior receipt or event log
immutability.negative_result_recorded: MV-G3-AXIS-CONTEXT-COMPARISON-001 stands as a negative causal result for the replicate-context (H1b) hypothesis; the 3-member context is NOT replaced merely to restore symmetry.

next_action: Phase B-F: build a NEW axis-neutral, paired-location (Z/Y/X triplet) generator that defines all three edges at each location independently of argmax-gradient, predeclare stratification, run methodological tests, then a small prospective review to test H3 vs H4.
